findings.text: Adjustment interface for a selected keeper that distinguishes a dedicated adjtime request from general mode-driven updates, records audit snapshots around changes, normalizes reported offset and time fields according to nanos versus micros selection, maps internal status to a result code with error override, and applies leap-second presentation tweaks near the scheduled leap boundary.

Registration helper that prepares the embedded semaphore, binds the clock character device to the shared file operation table, publishes the device, and propagates ownership from the driver operation table on success while reporting add failures.
Unregistration helper that detaches the character device, then marks the clock as defunct under exclusive access before releasing the remaining device reference.
Dynamic clock dispatch table that routes resolution, setting, reading and tuning requests to the per-clock helpers performing descriptor lookup and driver delegation.
Wall-clock snapshot helper that combines kept seconds with monotonic nanoseconds under a sequence guard and folds the sub-second part into the output structure.

Pulse entry for the core keeper that accepts phase and raw stamps, clears prior pulse error indications, announces signal presence, establishes a frequency base on initial call, validates pulse spacing, and then drives frequency-interval completion and phase correction.
Boot initialization that clears state for every keeper instance and then arms the real-time sync timer infrastructure or its no-op fallback.

Notification entry invoked on time jumps and sync events that cancels the pending sync timer when an offset jump occurred and otherwise queues background sync work when synchronized and no timer is pending; a header variant provides an empty fallback.
Early boot parameter parser that converts a string argument into a scaled tick adjustment for the core keeper and signals handled versus malformed input.
File operation entry points for dynamic clocks covering open with context allocation, release with driver teardown, plus read poll and ioctl delegation guarded by shared access and defunct checks.

Clock operation entry points for dynamic identifiers that resolve a descriptor, enforce write access for tuning and setting, validate strict time inputs where required, and delegate to driver callbacks or report unsupported operation.

Process CPU timer entry points that initialize group state with an optional profiling deadline derived from a resource limit and later refresh that profiling deadline under signal-hand protection after converting seconds to nanoseconds.

Real-time clock write gating computes a target moment by adding a caller-supplied sub-second offset minus a second to the current time, then accepts only targets landing within a small fuzz band near a second boundary, snapping accepted targets to the boundary and asking the caller to retry otherwise.

Hardware clock background worker does nothing unless synchronized and no sync timer is already queued, otherwise samples wall time, rejects samples outside the allowed window by rearming, adjusts for local-timezone clocks, prefers the legacy persistent setter and falls back to the RTC class, giving up silently when no hardware exists and otherwise rearming with success-aware delay selection.

RTC class update opens the configured system device, requires a set-time callback, and on initial observation of a device offset differing from the caller value stores the device value and asks for retry, only converting seconds to broken-down form and programming the hardware when offsets already agree.
Synchronized state is defined entirely by absence of the unsynchronized flag in the core keeper status word.

Status processing treats clearing of the phase-locked-loop flag as a drop to unsynchronized with leap schedule reset and pulse calibration restart, treats newly setting that flag as a reference-time capture, and otherwise preserves read-only bits while accepting only writable caller bits.

Mode-driven tuning dispatches each requested selector independently, handling nanos versus micros selection, scaled and clamped frequency with pulse-frequency refresh, clamped error bounds and time constant with nanos-dependent biasing, bounded TAI selection, offset integration, tick replacement, and a closing frequency recomputation when tick frequency or offset changed.

The adjustment path separates dedicated adjtime semantics, which swaps in a new adjustment and clears its fraction while preserving the old value for return, from general mode processing with audit bracketing, and always reports scaled frequency plus stored error bounds status constants and current driver pulse fields.

Leap-second presentation near or past the scheduled boundary remaps insertion and deletion announcements to outage or wait indications while nudging reported seconds and TAI offset to keep user-visible time continuous.
Pulse normalization folds timestamps with large sub-second remainder forward by a second while subtracting a full second worth of nanoseconds, yielding signed residuals centered near the boundary.

Phase filtering maintains a short shift register of recent corrections, reports the newest entry as the filtered value, and derives jitter as the magnitude of change between successive newest entries.

Frequency-interval control moves a shift exponent down on poor samples and up on good samples, clamping a counter at symmetric bounds and resetting it whenever the exponent steps, while respecting configured minimum and maximum exponents.

Frequency update rejects overlong intervals as errors with counter increment and interval shrink, otherwise computes a scaled raw offset, tracks wander against a threshold with distinct handling for good versus wandering samples, maintains an averaged stability metric, and only writes back to the system frequency when pulse-frequency steering is enabled and not held.

Phase update feeds negated error through the shift filter, discards samples whose jitter exceeds the adapted threshold scaled by a popcorn factor while counting them, otherwise optionally installs a scaled offset and cancels any running adjtime, then relaxes the jitter estimate toward the observed value.

Pulse handling clears jitter wander and error indications on each pulse, marks signal presence and validity, initializes the frequency base on the initial pulse, restarts calibration on out-of-range spacing with an error indication, advances the base and runs frequency update when the elapsed span reaches the averaging window, and always finishes with phase update.

Dynamic clock input-output paths acquire shared access, fail with device-missing when defunct or absent, delegate to optional driver callbacks with safe defaults for missing handlers, and always release the shared guard before returning.

Open validates non-defunct state under shared access before allocating a private context, unwinds cleanly on allocation or driver-open failure, links the context to file and clock with a device reference, while release invokes optional driver teardown, drops the device reference, frees the context and clears the file link.

Descriptor resolution converts an identifier to a file, requires the file operation table to match the dynamic-clock open handler with a present private context, then takes shared access and fails closed with reference cleanup on any mismatch.

Tuning and setting paths require write mode on the backing file and report access failure otherwise, setting additionally rejects non-strict timestamps before lookup, and clock operations report unsupported when the driver omits the corresponding callback.

Group initialization always resets timer state and only arms a profiling deadline when the supplied limit is finite, scaling the limit to nanoseconds, while limit refresh repeats that scaling and programs the profiling base under signal-hand protection.
Header guard marker denotes inclusion protection for internal NTP declarations.
Wall-clock sampling combines a sequence-begin and retry check in a loop to obtain a consistent seconds plus nanosecond reading, warning when called while timekeeping is suspended.

Dynamic clocks serialize input-output and open against unregistration with a reader-writer semaphore held for reading on all fast paths and for writing only when publishing the defunct mark, with registration initializing the guard before device publication.
Resource-limit refresh holds the target task signal-hand lock across programming of the profiling timer and reports lookup failure when the task cannot be locked.
Normalized pulse timestamp layout combines a signed wide seconds field with a signed long nanosecond residual that may be negative after folding.
Transient descriptor combines a borrowed file reference with the associated clock pointer obtained under shared access, released together by the matching put helper.
File operation table for dynamic clocks binds read poll ioctl open and release handlers with module ownership, exposing identical handling for native and compatibility ioctl paths.
Kernel clock dispatch structure for dynamic identifiers binds resolution setting reading and tuning slots to the descriptor-based helpers.

CMOS synchronization cycles among idle, work-queued and timer-armed conditions, where notification queues work when synchronized without a pending timer, the worker exits early on loss of sync or a queued timer and otherwise samples and rearms, and offset jumps cancel the timer outright.

Pulse frequency calibration progresses from uninitialized base through active averaging windows, restarting the base on initial pulse out-of-range pulses and completed windows, shrinking the window on errors and growing it on sustained good samples.

Phase-locked-loop status moves between disabled unsynchronized and enabled states, where disabling forces unsynchronized with leap reset and calibration restart while enabling captures a fresh reference time before merging caller status bits.

A notification racing the worker between timer expiry and rearm can queue redundant background work that exits immediately on observing a queued timer; the fragments describe this as harmless but wasteful.

Hardware programming applies a timezone shift for local clocks and programs only the seconds portion through broken-down conversion, so samples must already sit near a boundary and the initial RTC-class attempt intentionally reports retry to learn the device offset.

Pulse handling treats initial-sample base establishment, out-of-range spacing and overlong frequency spans as distinct restart paths with different status bits and counters, so callers cannot assume every pulse contributes to frequency or phase.

Default hardware sync offset equals half of the per-second nanosecond count [CITED], and the acceptance fuzz equals five tick intervals in nanoseconds [CITED], with accepted targets snapped to a boundary.
Resource-limit conversion scales seconds by the nanoseconds-per-second factor [CITED], and process CPU profiling uses that scaled deadline only when the limit differs from infinity.

Hardware setters report missing-device when no implementation exists and the RTC path reports retry while learning offsets, while dynamic clock polling signals an error mask on descriptor failure and setting enforces write access with unsupported fallback.
